chapter: The Latin scene and business of the 1940s-70s
title: The conga craze and the original La Conga club
summary: He dates the conga in New York and Desi Arnaz in Too Many Girls.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Where did the Conga come in here?
The conga music?
Yeah.
Way back.
Oh, yeah. Before then.
In New York?
Oh, yeah. They got rid of popular music.
That's what I'm talking about, because Desi Arnez and his (unintelligible) that he introduced --
Oh, no, no, no, no, please, no. No. That's why I say, there are too many things that -- conga music hit heavy in Paris.
Yeah.

Then they opened a club there in 19 -- well, wait a minute, let me put everything in the respective order, because I'm bad on dates. Conga was playing here in the '30s. Then came (unintelligible) went to work with a show that was produced in Paris --
Richard Rodgers --
No, no. I saw him on television the other day, he had a show (unintelligible). Georgie Abbott.
It was a show called Too Many Girls.
Tha's right, Rodgers wrote the music.
They had two nightly feature there.
Desi Arnaz was (unintelligible).
He did Spic 'n Spanish, right? That was in 1939, I can tell you exactly, that was in October, 1939.

Right in there, almost -- I don't know who was in, a day before, a month before or a month after. They opened in Martinique (unintelligible) they opened a club. A fellow friend of mine opened the club called the La Conga. And one of those guys that was involved was a good friend and a good tap dancer, a dancer called Eleanor Powell.
Eleanor Powell?
Yeah. And she was like a hostess every night. I don't know if she was (unintelligible), I don't know. It was a __________ relation.
Yeah.
(Unintelligible) and then the other -- (unintelligible) La Rosa Orchestra.
When was this, 1940?
'38, I think, like.
What was the __________ orchestra? Was that basically a sweet orchestra?
No, no, no, (unintelligible). And the only thing that was exciting was the Conga, and everybody formed
the conga lines.
I know that (unintelligible) La Conga was published in 1938.
Yes.
